family.description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes. This domain shows structural similarity to TIR domains. This domain is found within the TEP1 (Telomerase protein component 1) protein.
family.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4062)

history.description:
Created the first overlay for PF13271 (DUF4062) from a 2026 bioRxiv preprint
(PMID:42146377, CC BY 4.0, NOT peer reviewed) plus local sequence analysis.

Two MECHANISTIC causal graphs, each with hash-checked source extracts:

1. tep1-duf4062-domain-nad-hydrolysis. Human TEP1 (UniProtKB:Q99973, PF13271 at
   901-1015) hydrolyses NAD+ and NADP+ to ADP-ribose or ADP-ribose phosphate plus
   nicotinamide; the isolated DUF4062-containing construct TEP1 886-1113 is
   sufficient; activity depends on Glu1008; reconstituted MVP+TEP1 vaults are active
   and E1008A vaults are not. Grounded: the retrieved sequence confirms residue 1008
   is Glu and 908/954/976 are Arg, all inside the Pfam interval. Coordinate limit
   recorded, the tested construct is wider than the interval at both ends.

2. kpswz-portal-triggered-nad-depletion. The Klebsiella DUF4062 protein the authors
   name Swarozyc hydrolyses NAD+ only with the phage Bas14 portal protein and Glu97;
   infected cells expressing it lose NAD+ while E97A cells do not; phage defence in
   E. coli required Glu97 and the auxiliary domain, with protection at low and culture
   collapse at high multiplicity. Nodes are deliberately ungrounded: the tested
   sequences are only in the preprint's supplementary material, which was not
   inspected, so no accession is asserted and E97 is not placed on a PF13271 interval.
   The authors' proposed TIR-repositioning step is observed only by modelling and was
   deliberately left out of the graph.

Two OPEN discussions:
- duf4062-ntpase-label-versus-adjacent-nacht (INTERPRETATION): orthogroup labels such
  as COG5635 transfer an NTPase label from large relatives whose NACHT domain is
  adjacent to, not part of, DUF4062. In a 2026-10-30 UniProtKB snapshot a P-loop
  domain co-occurs with DUF4062 in 85.9% of proteins over 450 aa but 1.3% of those of
  450 aa or less.
- short-bacterial-duf4062-activity-and-trigger (CURATION_TODO): whether a short
  stand-alone bacterial member is actually an active NADase. UniProtKB:Q31PW6
  (Synpcc7942_0873, PF13271 at 6-146 of 362 aa) retains the family's most conserved
  Glu at Glu83 (93% of 375 short bacterial homologs; Pfam HMM state 78, P(E)=0.602)
  and has no Walker A or Walker B motif. No causal edge is curated for it, because
  conservation is not activity and three of four human paralogues assayed were
  inactive.

Evidence extracts at evidence/PF13271/ with SHA-256 recorded: the preprint
quotations (minimal, attributed, CC BY 4.0), the TEP1 identity/coordinate check, and
the Synpcc7942_0873 identity and motif analysis.

Also regenerated the KGX and SSSOM interchange files with `just exports --apply`;
the only change is PF13271's curation_status, SEEDED to IN_PROGRESS, one line each.

Checks: `just records --apply`, `just validate-all`, `just sources-check` (0 errors;
its 16 warnings also occur on an unmodified tree), `just causal-graphs --apply`.
Remaining: `just qc` fails on the Pages site-source pin ledger for
data/families/PF13271.yaml, which per docs/records.md needs an authorized source
checkpoint captured against a published commit; that publication step was not
authorized here and no pin was invented. Two test_review_research_runtime failures
also occur on an unmodified tree in this environment (LinkML loader lock).

Limits: all functional evidence is a single preprint; no experiment has been done on
Q31PW6; Glu83 is positioned by family conservation and the Pfam HMM, not by alignment
to the tested Klebsiella sequence; the Evangelion preprint
(doi:10.64898/2026.06.25.731849) was not inspected; the UniProtKB counts are one
snapshot. Imported identity, counters and seed classification are unchanged, and the
record is IN_PROGRESS, not reviewed. Contributed from a KBase gene-annotate dashboard
review of CP088958.1_900 (ai4curation/ai-gene-review PR 5756).
history.summary: Create PF13271 (DUF4062) overlay: two mechanistic NAD+-hydrolase causal graphs (human TEP1; Klebsiella portal-activated Swarozyc) and two open discussions on the NTPase label and short bacterial members

causal_graphs.context: Full-length human NWD1, NWD2, NPHP3 and TEP1 were purified from HEK293F cells, incubated with NAD+ and NADP+, and reaction products analysed by HPLC. Of those four, only TEP1 was active. The isolated TEP1 886-1113 construct was assayed separately. Vaults were reconstituted with MVP and TEP1, or TEP1 E1008A, in HEK293F cells and assayed for NADase and NADPase activity.

evidence.explanation: Establishes that the DUF4062-containing region alone carries the activity, which is what ties the chemistry to this Pfam family rather than to the NACHT or WD40 regions of TEP1. The companion quotation in the same extract reports the products and the three inactive paralogues. The construct is slightly wider than the Pfam interval, as recorded in family_mapping.
evidence.snippet: The isolated DUF4062 domain (TEP1886–1113, hereafter TEP1TIR) was sufficient to hydrolyze NAD+ and NADP+

evidence.explanation: Grounds the tested protein on this Pfam family and supplies the coordinate limits. Identity grounding only; it carries no causal weight of its own.

edges.mechanism: The purified protein converts NAD+ and NADP+ to ADP-ribose, or ADP-ribose phosphate, plus nicotinamide, and the isolated DUF4062-containing construct is sufficient for this, which localises the hydrolytic activity to that region rather than to the other domains of the full-length protein. This is a directly observed in vitro product measurement, not a demonstration of the reaction in cells.
edges.subject: tep1-duf4062-catalytic-region

evidence.explanation: The same sentence reports the products and the E1008 dependence. It also records that NWD1, NWD2 and NPHP3 were inactive, which is retained in the limitations of this graph rather than treated as support for the family.
evidence.snippet: Only TEP1 hydrolyzed NAD+ and NADP+, producing ADP-ribose or ADP-ribose phosphate (ADPRP) and nicotinamide (NAM) with activity dependent on the active site E1008

evidence.explanation: Confirms against the retrieved sequence that residue 1008 of Q99973 is a glutamate inside the PF13271 interval, so the numbering used by the source refers to the domain of this family. Identity check only.
evidence.snippet: position 1008 = E (the substituted active-site glutamate, E1008A)

edges.mechanism: Substituting the conserved active-site glutamate abolishes product formation in the purified-protein assay. This identifies Glu1008 as required for the measured hydrolysis under these conditions. It does not by itself establish the chemical role of the residue, since a substitution can also perturb local structure.
edges.subject: tep1-e1008a

evidence.explanation: Pairs the wild-type and active-site-mutant particles in one comparison, which is why the activity is assigned to the DUF4062 site of TEP1 rather than to a co-purifying contaminant. The products on the particle were not separately itemised in the retained extract, so the shared product node is used at the NAD(P)ase level.
evidence.snippet: Purified vaults containing TEP1, but not the E1008A mutant, displayed NADase and NADPase activities

edges.mechanism: Vaults reconstituted with TEP1 show NADase and NADPase activity, and those carrying the E1008A protein do not, so the activity measured on the assembled particle is conferred by the same TEP1 active site. This is an observed activity of a reconstituted particle. It does not establish that vaults hydrolyse NAD+ at a physiologically relevant rate in cells.
edges.subject: reconstituted-vault-with-tep1

causal_graphs.family_mapping: UniProtKB:Q99973 is 2627 residues with a single Pfam:PF13271 interval at 901-1015, inclusive. The retrieved sequence confirms the source's numbering, with residue 1008 a glutamate and residues 908, 954 and 976 arginines, all inside that interval. Coordinate limit, the tested catalytic construct TEP1 886-1113 extends 15 residues before and 98 residues after the PF13271 interval, so the measured activity maps to a region containing the DUF4062 domain rather than strictly to the Pfam interval. The NACHT, P-loop and WD40 regions of Q99973 lie outside 901-1015 and are not the object of this result.
causal_graphs.limitations: The sole source is a bioRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed. The reported kinetics are slow, with an apparent Km near 6.9 mM for NADP+ and undeterminable for NAD+, and specific activity rising with enzyme concentration, so no physiological turnover rate is established and oligomerisation-dependent activation remains an interpretation. Three of the four human DUF4062-NACHT paralogues assayed were inactive, so this result does not transfer to other family members. No elementary chemical step, proton transfer or substrate-binding geometry is resolved here, and the biological role of the vault is unresolved. Figure panels and raw chromatograms were not inspected; the quotations come from the abstract and results text.

nodes.label: Purified human TEP1 DUF4062-containing catalytic region with NAD+ or NADP+
HPLC-detected ADP-ribose or ADP-ribose phosphate plus nicotinamide
TEP1 E1008A substitution replacing the wild-type active-site glutamate
Human vault reconstituted from MVP and TEP1, assayed for NAD(P)ase activity

causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant full-length human TEP1 (UniProtKB:Q99973), its isolated DUF4062-containing construct TEP1 886-1113, the E1008A substitution, and human vaults reconstituted from MVP plus TEP1. This is one tested protein, not a family-wide property, and not endogenous regulation of TEP1 in cells.
causal_graphs.title: The human TEP1 DUF4062 domain hydrolyses NAD+ and NADP+ and depends on Glu1008

causal_graphs.context: Five DUF4062 proteins lying in predicted antiphage defence islands were expressed in E. coli BW25113 and challenged with phages from the BASEL library. Liquid cultures expressing KpSwz were infected with phage Bas14 at high and low multiplicity, and cellular NAD+ was measured. Purified KpSwz was incubated with NAD+ with and without the Bas14 portal protein, and products were analysed by HPLC-UV.

evidence.explanation: A single in vitro reaction establishes both the portal requirement and the active-site requirement, so the activation is a measured dependency rather than an inference from the structures. The accession of the tested protein is unresolved, as recorded in family_mapping.
evidence.snippet: this activity required the active-site residue E97 and portalBas14

edges.mechanism: Purified KpSwz hydrolyses NAD+ only in the presence of the Bas14 portal protein, and the reaction also requires Glu97. The portal therefore acts as the activating ligand of an otherwise quiescent enzyme, which is consistent with the autoinhibited head-to-head assembly seen by cryo-EM. The structural route from portal binding to an active site is proposed by the authors rather than observed, and is not asserted here.
edges.subject: bas14-portal-protein

evidence.explanation: The wild-type arm of the same comparison supplies this edge. The mutant arm is recorded separately, so the active-site dependency is not counted twice as independent support.
evidence.snippet: NAD+ levels were reduced upon phage infection in cells expressing WT KpSwz, but not the E97A mutant

edges.mechanism: Cells expressing wild-type KpSwz lose NAD+ on phage infection. Taken with the in vitro reaction, this places the hydrolytic activity as the cause of the drop in the cellular pool. The measurement is a population average and does not resolve timing within single infected cells.
edges.subject: kpswz-nadase-activity

evidence.explanation: Pairs wild type and active-site mutant in the same infection experiment, which is what connects the in vitro chemistry to an event inside infected cells. It does not by itself show that the loss of NAD+ causes the death of those cells.
evidence.snippet: NAD+ levels were reduced upon phage infection in cells expressing WT KpSwz, but not the E97A mutant

edges.mechanism: Cells expressing the E97A protein do not lose NAD+ on infection, so the active-site glutamate is required for the depletion. A substitution can also perturb folding, so this identifies a requirement rather than a chemical role for the residue.
edges.subject: kpswz-e97a

evidence.explanation: A genetic requirement measured as a plating or growth phenotype, which is why directness is recorded as INDIRECT, since the steps between NAD+ depletion and population-level protection are not individually resolved. The retained extract also records the multiplicity-dependent outcome underlying the abortive-infection interpretation.
evidence.snippet: Phage defense required the active site E97 of K. pneumoniae DUF4062 and its auxiliary domain

edges.mechanism: Phage defence in the heterologous host required both Glu97 and the auxiliary domain of the protein, so the catalytic site and the sensor region are each necessary for protection. Protection was seen at low multiplicity of infection while high multiplicity collapsed the culture, which is the pattern expected of abortive infection rather than of direct phage inhibition.
edges.subject: kpswz-nadase-activity

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The source identifies the tested protein as a DUF4062-containing protein of Klebsiella pneumoniae, recovered in its own DUF4062 family search, and numbers its active-site glutamate E97. Coordinate limit, the sequences and accessions of the five tested bacterial proteins are given only in the supplementary material of the preprint, which was not inspected, so no UniProt or NCBI accession is asserted here and E97 is not placed on a PF13271 interval. The nodes of this graph are therefore deliberately ungrounded, and the domain assignment rests on the family search of the authors rather than on an independently checked match.
causal_graphs.limitations: The sole source is a bioRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed. Because the tested sequence is unresolved, the mapping of E97 onto the Pfam domain is the assignment of the authors and was not independently verified. Defence was assayed in a heterologous E. coli host, so the native Klebsiella phenotype is untested. The escaper-mutation and cryo-EM results support portal recognition as the trigger, but the authors describe the final step, repositioning of the TIR-like domains into an active conformation, as a proposal supported by modelling rather than an observed transition, and that step is deliberately absent from this graph. Whether cell death follows from NAD+ loss alone is not resolved. Nothing here transfers to short DUF4062 proteins in other lineages, including cyanobacteria.

nodes.label: Phage Bas14 portal protein presented to KpSwz
Infection-triggered loss of the cellular NAD+ pool
KpSwz E97A substitution replacing the wild-type active-site glutamate
Protection of the bacterial population against phage, by abortive infection

causal_graphs.scope: The Klebsiella pneumoniae DUF4062 protein the source names Swarozyc (KpSwz), expressed in Escherichia coli BW25113, with its E97A substitution and its auxiliary domain, challenged with phage Bas14 or co-expressed with the Bas14 portal protein. The tested object is that single protein in a heterologous host. Neither the native Klebsiella context nor other family members are covered.
causal_graphs.title: A Klebsiella DUF4062 protein depletes NAD+ on phage portal recognition and aborts infection

record.description: This presumed domain is functionally uncharacterised. This domain family is found in bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes. This domain shows structural similarity to TIR domains. This domain is found within the TEP1 (Telomerase protein component 1) protein.

evidence.explanation: Places the NACHT ATPase as a domain adjacent to DUF4062 in the human proteins, and reports NAD+ hydrolysis as the activity of the domain itself. It does not test NTP hydrolysis by any DUF4062 domain, so it narrows the architectural question without closing it.

The co-occurrence counts retained with the candidate's identity analysis show the P-loop domain tracking the long architecture. They are a single API snapshot of InterPro cross-references, not a curated classification, and will drift with releases.

discussions.notes: Raised while reviewing a KBase gene-annotate dashboard call for Synechococcus elongatus CP088958.1_900, which was annotated a putative NACHT-family NTPase from its COG5635 orthogroup (ai4curation/ai-gene-review PR 5756).
discussions.prompt: Should a short stand-alone DUF4062 protein be annotated as an NTPase because its orthogroup is labelled a NACHT NTPase?
discussions.rationale: Orthogroup labels such as COG5635, "Predicted NTPase, NACHT family domain", group short stand-alone DUF4062 proteins together with large multidomain relatives in which the NTP-hydrolysing NACHT domain is a separate domain adjacent to DUF4062. Automated pipelines transfer the NTPase label across that boundary. In a UniProtKB snapshot taken on 2026-10-30, a P-loop NTPase domain (IPR027417) co-occurs with DUF4062 in 2514 of 2925 proteins over 450 aa, or 85.9%, but in only 23 of 1720 proteins of 450 aa or less, or 1.3%, and NACHT itself in one. The activity reported for the domain is NAD+ hydrolysis, a different chemistry from NTP hydrolysis. This bears on how DUFMech should treat orthogroup-derived functional labels generally. It is not resolved here, and no NTPase activity has been tested for or excluded in any short member.

evidence.explanation: Supplies the chemistry of the family, the catalytic glutamate and the portal-triggered mechanism for the tested proteins, and the inactive human paralogues that keep the question open. No cyanobacterial member was tested, and the source is a preprint.

Grounds the identity of the candidate, its domain interval and the Glu83 position through two independent estimates, pairwise conservation across 375 homologs and the Pfam profile HMM. Sequence analysis only. It establishes that the residue is present, not that the protein is active.

discussions.notes: Open leads. Align the KpSwz sequence from the supplementary material of the preprint to place Glu83 against the tested E97 directly, which would also let the nodes of that graph be grounded. Inspect the companion Evangelion preprint (doi:10.64898/2026.06.25.731849), which reports a putative catalytic Glu87 in a plasmid-borne DUF4062 defence system. Assess whether the neighbouring SNF2/RAD54-family helicase and UvrC-like endonuclease genes of Synpcc7942_0873 form a defence island, which was not examined. Contributed from a KBase gene-annotate dashboard review (ai4curation/ai-gene-review PR 5756). Imported identity, counters and seed classification are unchanged.
discussions.prompt: Is a short stand-alone bacterial DUF4062 protein such as Synechococcus elongatus Synpcc7942_0873 an active NADase, and what activates it?
discussions.rationale: The tested bacterial proteins were chosen because they lie in defence islands and share a similar C-terminal auxiliary domain, and activation ran through a phage portal protein. UniProtKB:Q31PW6 (Synpcc7942_0873) has the same compact layout, with PF13271 at 6-146 of 362 residues, a predicted coiled coil at 170-197 and an unassigned C-terminal region, and it retains the most conserved glutamate of the family at Glu83. That residue is identical in 93% of 375 short bacterial homologs and sits at Pfam HMM match state 78, whose consensus residue is a highly conserved E with emission probability 0.602. The protein has no Walker A or Walker B motif. None of that is activity. The family is not uniformly catalytic, since three of four human paralogues assayed were inactive, so conservation of the glutamate cannot settle whether this protein is an enzyme, and no causal edge is curated for it. Resolving it needs an assay, not more sequence analysis.

record.name: Domain of unknown function (DUF4062)
